idea: Why water pipes make unusual noises
title: Understanding Pipe Noise: From Knocking to Whistling
description: Unusual pipe noises are usually your plumbing system signaling a specific mechanical issue. A sharp banging sound when a faucet or valve closes—known as water hammer—occurs when moving water suddenly stops, sending shockwaves through the line. Installing water hammer arrestors absorbs this hydraulic shock. Rattling or thumping typically points to loose pipe straps along wall studs or floor joists, allowing pipes to physically vibrate against wood framing. Whistling or humming often indicates high incoming water pressure or worn valve washers. Addressing these sounds early prevents joint stress, pipe fatigue, and leaks. Consult a licensed plumber to test water pressure and secure loose supply lines.
